column3: NKJV takes the word glossed “head” as a name, “the prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal”; it can also be read “the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.”
NKJV again renders “the chief prince” as “the prince of Rosh,” taking the word as a name.
Close to the Hebrew; “clothed in perfection” is rendered “splendidly clothed.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Cush and Put” is rendered “Ethiopia, and Libya.”
Close to the Hebrew; “you will be mustered” is rendered “you will be visited,” and “a land restored from the sword” “the land of those brought back from the sword.”
Close to the Hebrew; “words will come up on your heart” is rendered “thoughts will arise in your mind.”
Close to the Hebrew; “at the navel of the earth” is rendered “in the midst of the land.”
Close to the Hebrew; “years” is rendered “for years.”
Close to the Hebrew; “my rage will rise up in my nostrils” is rendered “My fury will show in My face.”
Close to the Hebrew; “against him” is rendered “against Gog.”
Close to the Hebrew; “blood” is rendered “bloodshed.”
